Alta: $80 Million In Total Funding Advances Institutional Blockchain Infrastructure
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 6:38 PM
Alta: $80 Million In Total Funding Advances Institutional Blockchain Infrastructure
Alta has raised $80 million in total funding, including a $47.5 million Series A led by Index Ventures, to develop blockchain infrastructure designed for regulated financial institutions. GV, Blackbird Ventures, Square Peg and Capital 49 participated in the Series A. The total also includes $32.5 million in previous seed financing.
Alta is building infrastructure that allows financial assets and products to move globally and programmatically, with privacy, compliance, identity and authorization controls incorporated into the blockchain itself.
Its architecture uses recursive zero-knowledge cryptography to verify that transactions meet required rules while keeping balances, transaction details, identities and compliance policies private. The company intends the system to support activity across assets, blockchain networks and jurisdictions.
Airwallex has selected Alta as a technology partner, connecting its global payments infrastructure with Alta’s blockchain. The collaboration will support stablecoin pay-ins and payouts, alongside connectivity to local fiat payment networks across 200 countries and 90 currencies.
Alta positions its infrastructure as a neutral foundation that banks, payment providers and other financial institutions can use to develop services.
Its first product will focus on corporate liquidity management. Built around tokenized assets, the offering is intended to enable just-in-time funding, improve foreign exchange efficiency and reduce the cash businesses keep in prefunded accounts.
The product will also allow businesses to move into and out of yield-bearing tokenized assets, helping them earn interest on capital that would otherwise remain idle. Alta cited an estimated $4 trillion held in prefunded accounts globally as evidence of the opportunity to improve capital efficiency.
The company’s founders include CEO Loong Wang, President Catherine Porter and Airwallex Co-Founder and CEO Jack Zhang. They identified institutional controls and connectivity as requirements for expanding blockchain-based finance, including transactions initiated by AI agents.
Alta will use the funding to continue developing its blockchain, expand institutional partnerships and global financial connectivity, and grow its engineering and compliance teams.
KEY QUOTES
“Existing blockchains aren’t designed for the privacy and compliance requirements of global financial institutions. We’re taking a fundamentally different approach, building privacy, programmable compliance, and identity and authorization directly into the blockchain. This will enable money and assets to move instantly, globally, and securely, whether it’s a bank settling a transaction or an AI agent making a payment.”
Loong Wang, Co-Founder And CEO Of Alta
“Technology alone won’t be enough to modernize global finance. Financial institutions need infrastructure they can trust, with clear controls over who they’re transacting with, where money can move, and how sensitive information is protected. As AI agents increasingly make financial decisions and execute transactions, that trust becomes even more critical. Privacy, compliance, and accountability just aren’t barriers to innovation – they’re what will allow it to scale.”

articles.title: Enza Capital is raising up to $80 Million to bet on African AI Startups
articles.snippet: Enza Capital is raising up to $80 Million to bet on African AI Startups Innovation Village
articles.text:
Enza Capital is raising up to $80 Million to bet on African AI Startups
0
By
Smart Megwai
on
November 11, 2026
Africa , Business , Funding , Investments , Startups
Enza Capital has secured a first close of $21 million for its third fund, Enza Capital III LP, which it will dedicate entirely to artificial-intelligence startups across Africa.
The pan-African venture firm, which has offices in Nairobi, Johannesburg and Cairo, is targeting $60 million for the fund with a hard cap of $80 million, and expects a final close in about a year, the firm said in an emailed statement .
The fund’s entire thesis rests on a gap. African AI, by the report’s account, attracts relatively little venture capital despite growing interest in its potential. Investors deployed about $46.8 million into African AI startups through 2026, the report says, concentrated mostly in fintech and risk-intelligence companies and modest next to AI investment in other regions.
A Briter Bridges report cited in the report found that 30% of surveyed African AI companies are entirely bootstrapped, with funding clustered among more established players; some founders say investors’ preference for proven traction makes it harder for early-stage AI companies to raise money at all.
Enza Capital is betting that the gap in African AI funding is a market failure to be exploited, not a verdict on the sector’s potential.
Enza Capital’s existing investments span SeamlessHR, Money254, Sendy, Gigmile and Peach Payments, giving a sense of the firm’s range before this fund narrows its focus specifically to AI.
That earlier spread, across HR tech, personal finance, logistics and payments, suggests Enza Capital III LP will be looking for AI applied across similarly varied sectors rather than betting narrowly on one vertical.
What to watch
The first thing to consider is the pace over the next 12 months. To move from a target of $21 million to a goal of $60 million, and even aiming for a hard cap of $80 million, it will be essential to convince limited partners that the funding gap in African AI is investable rather than simply an indicator that the market has already assessed the associated risks.
The second point to consider is whether the fund’s eventual portfolio will focus primarily on fintech and risk-intelligence companies, which have already attracted most of the continent’s AI capital, or if it will genuinely explore newer categories that the report indicates are currently underfunded and lacking institutional investment.

articles.title: Course Corrected Raises €80 Million to Back European Energy and Resource Transition Startups
articles.snippet: Course Corrected Raises €80 Million to Back European Energy and Resource Transition Startups ESG Today
articles.text:
Energy Transition / Private Equity & Venture Capital
Course Corrected Raises €80 Million to Back European Energy and Resource Transition Startups
Kenny Fisher
November 12, 2026
Venture capital investor Course Corrected announced today that it has raised €80 million (USD$89 million) at the final close of its second fund, focused on investing in early-stage European technology companies across the energy and resource transition.
Founded in 2021 by Christine Ahlstrand, Kerstin Cooley and Katja Bergman, Stockholm-based Course Corrected invests in early-stage technology companies developing solutions to enable industries to become more energy, resource and cost efficient. Fund II builds on the firm’s first fund, which focused entirely on climate tech.
According to the firm, Fund II will invest in 20 – 30 companies across key themes including energy systems, industrial optimization and automation, electrification and resource-smart solutions, focusing on scalable businesses whose products advance the energy and resource transition.
Kerstin Cooley, founding partner at Course Corrected, said:
“We invest to generate strong financial returns. Impact is how we get there: by backing juggernauts that solve real problems, scale commercially, and transform industries for the better.”
Fund II invests only in European companies. Course Corrected noted that the fund’s close amidst a need for Europe to channel more of its savings into European businesses, noting that only a small fraction of pension and insurance assets are allocated to venture capital, and that more than half of EU venture funds’ investments are directed to startups outside of the EU.
Christine Ahlstrand, founding partner at Course Corrected, said:
“Europe has the research, the technology, the founders and the markets. But who will own the next generation of industry if we do not finance the companies building it?”
To date, Fund II has made seven investments, including Tavion, Renasens, eComID and Skye.
Investors in the fund include the European Investment Fund (EIF), which committed €35 million, Swedish state-owned venture capital investor Saminvest, pension investors SEB Life & Pension and SEB-Stiftelsen, a Swedish foundation and private investors.
Pontus Bergekrans, CIO at SEB Life & Pension AB, said:
“We believe Europe has the talent and innovation needed to lead the energy transition. Course Corrected combines a strong team, a focused strategy and access to companies addressing some of the region’s most important challenges.”

FinTech Funding October 2026: Indian FinTechs raise USD 76 million across 6 deals
The largest deal of the month came from Even, which raised USD 50 million from Khosla Ventures and Alpha Wave Global, followed by StockGro and Fission Labs, which raised USD 10 million each.
Shrishti Sharma
ETBFSI
Published On Nov 11, 2026 at 06:07 PM IST

Indian FinTechs raised USD 76 million across six equity funding rounds in October 2026, according to data collated by Tracxn.
The month witnessed funding activity across healthcare and insurance technology, investment and trading platforms, blockchain-based financial infrastructure, lending and debt resolution, and cross-border payments .
The largest deal of the month came from Even, a healthcare platform offering managed care services, doctor consultations and health insurance solutions, which raised USD 50 million in a Series B round from Khosla Ventures and Alpha Wave Global.
This was followed by StockGro, a stock market advisory and research platform, which raised USD 10 million in a Series B round from Aart Corporate Advisors.
Advt
Another notable transaction was Fission Labs , a financial technology company building blockchain-based infrastructure for tokenised investment funds, which raised USD 10 million in a Series A round. The round saw participation from Pantera Capital, Circle, Borderless Capital, New Form Capital, gCC, Manhattan Venture Partners, Reflexive Capital and Lattice, along with angel investors Ari Rubenstein and Anthony Scaramucci.
Together, the three largest transactions accounted for USD 70 million, or nearly 92 per cent of the total funding raised during October.
Among the other deals during the month:
Tradl, an artificial intelligence-powered trading platform, raised USD 4 million in a seed funding round from Stellaris Venture Partners.
CredFix, a financial technology platform connecting lenders and borrowers, particularly those facing financial distress, raised USD 2 million in a seed round from Stargazer Growth and Tanglin Venture Partners.
Saber, a provider of stablecoin-powered cross-border payment infrastructure, also raised an undisclosed amount in a seed funding round from Tether and Titan.
Funding activity in October was lower than the previous month, with total funding declining to USD 76 million across six deals, compared with USD 111 million across 10 deals in September 2026.

China Physical AI Roundup: UniX AI Raises $75M Pre-A, Plus TensorWorld, UBTech Order and Huawei CloudRobo
By Greg Bock · 17 November 2026 · 5 min read
Insider Brief
Chinese robotics companies attracted new funding and commercial orders across humanoids, robot components and physical AI, led by UniX AI’s 500 million yuan (about $75 million) Pre-A round.
TensorWorld raised more than $100 million across two early funding rounds, while robot-chip developer XiXuan Chuangzhi secured 500 million yuan (about $75 million) at a 4 billion yuan post-money valuation.
UBTech secured an order for 400 humanoid robots, Huawei Cloud released an open-source robot world model, and TARS and Robotera reported industrial and logistics deployments.
China ‘s robotics companies continue drawing fresh investment in humanoids , robot chips and training models, led by UniX AI’s 500 million yuan (about $75 million) Pre-A round. Other developments include a 400-unit UBTech humanoid order, Hesai’s third-quarter results and Huawei Cloud’s release of an open-source robot world model .
UniX AI
UniX AI , which makes wheeled humanoid robots for security, hotels and retail, has raised 500 million yuan (about $75 million) in a Pre-A round, Science and Technology Daily reported , citing the Suzhou company. Existing investors Xienuo and Yonghua added to their stakes. New backers include Greenland Group, a customer that joined as a strategic investor, along with Keli Sensing, HUST Ventures and others. UniX said it ships more than 100 robots a month, with peak monthly output above 300, and has batch orders from property groups, Certis and Inspur. Proceeds will fund algorithm research, product updates and wider use in property management, hotels and retail.
TensorWorld
TensorWorld, which was founded in July and is building physics-based foundation models that predict how objects move and interact, has raised more than $100 million across an angel round and an angel-plus round, according to a Starlink Capital post published by 36Kr . Cathay Capital and HongShan co-led the angel round, with IDG Capital, CDH VGC, Starlink Capital and Ant Group participating. Ant Group, Heyu Capital and Meituan Strategic co-led the later round.
XiXuan Chuangzhi
XiXuan Chuangzhi, a robot-chip company set up in May by UBTech, MetaX and Fenglong, closed a 500 million yuan (about $75 million) angel round at a 4 billion yuan (about $600 million) post-money valuation, China Securities Journal reported , citing a UBTech WeChat post. GGV Capital and Matrix Partners China co-led the round. Funds will go to chip and platform research, a software toolchain, hiring and joint testing with robot makers. XiXuan plans a development platform in 2027 and its first system-on-chip in 2028. MetaX is a listed chip designer.
UBTech
UBTech signed an agreement for Yongda Auto to buy 400 of its U1 Pro ultra-bionic humanoids, with delivery planned this year, NBD reported . NBD said it was UBTech’s first disclosed large order for that line. The robots will be used for product demonstrations, sales and customer service, and the partners plan a Shanghai showroom. The contract value was undisclosed. UBTech also signed a pact with Tianyi Telecom Terminal, a China Telecom unit, setting a three-year goal of more than 1 million home-companion robots and 100,000 ultra-bionic or wheeled humanoid terminals, IT Home reported . Those figures are market targets, not a firm purchase order.

articles.snippet: Funding and M&A Roundup: Green Genius Raises $72.5 Million Via Green Bonds Mercom Capital Group
articles.text:
November 11, 2026
Staff
Solar , Storage
Renewable energy project developer Green Genius has completed a €65 million (~$72.5 million) green bond issue to refinance existing subordinated construction loans. The bonds have a four-year maturity and carry a floating interest rate based on the three-month Euro Interbank Offered Rate (EURIBOR) plus 8% annually. They are expected to be admitted to trading on the Sustainable Bond List of Nasdaq Stockholm.
FluoRok, a U.K.-based company developing materials for applications including lithium-ion battery electrolytes , has raised $30 million in an oversubscribed Series A funding round to scale its manufacturing platform and expand fluorochemical production. Orano Venture Fund and Supernova Invest led the funding round, with participation from Bidra Innovation Ventures.
RadianX, a perovskite solar module manufacturer formerly known as California Perovskite Technology, has raised $9 million in combined venture and project financing to scale production of its certified perovskite solar modules. SOSV and Twynam co-led the seed funding round, with participation from One Small Planet, Sahsen Ventures, Avila VC, California Innovation Fund, quantumEDGE, Riceberg Ventures, and Alumni Ventures.
ARRAY Technologies, a provider of solar tracking technology, fixed-tilt products, and foundation solutions, and Shoals Technologies Group , a provider of electrical balance-of-system solutions for utility-scale solar and battery storage, have entered into a definitive agreement for a stock-for-stock merger. Under the merger agreement, ARRAY will be the legal acquirer and corporate parent of the combined company, and Shoals shareholders will receive 1.6931 ARRAY shares for each Shoals share they own.
SOLV Energy, a company that provides construction, operation, and maintenance services for large-scale solar and battery storage projects, has acquired Texas-based ASB Energy Services, a contractor specializing in substation foundations, civil construction, and battery energy storage infrastructure, for approximately $45 million. The transaction comprises $36 million in cash and $9 million in shares of SOLV Energy’s Class A common stock, excluding customary closing adjustments.

This is your weekly news roundup, which takes a quick look at some developments in government, politics, education, environment and other topics across El Paso.
Record Number of Donors Gave UTEP Historic $70 Million in Fiscal Year 2026
The University of Texas at El Paso reported a record $70 million in philanthropic support during the 2025-26 fiscal year that ended Aug. 31. UTEP officials said the money would be used to support initiatives that benefit students, faculty and aspects of campus life.
The university’s previous record was $50.5 million in fiscal year 2024. The institution also reported that the 6,703 donors were the most in school history. UTEP recorded 6,428 donors in fiscal year 2024-25.
Among the major donations during 2026 fiscal year were the record $30 million from UTEP alumnus Miguel A. “Mike” Loya in February for engineering scholarships, $5 million from Tawney, Acosta and Chaparro, and $5 million from the Paul L. Foster Family Foundation in a matching gift for the planned UTEP law school, and $1.5 million from University Medical Center and $1.1 million from the Hospitals of Providence and Tenet Healthcare Foundation to enhance healthcare education.
There also were donations to the Athletics Department of $2.5 million from Paul L. Foster and Alejandra de la Vega Foster, and $1 million each from Frank and Shirley Sloan and Bob McFadden.
The university said in a news release that the money raised would go toward athletics, student scholarships, campus enhancements, faculty recruitment and retention, academic and research initiatives and other strategic priorities.
UTEP President Heather Wilson said the historic level of philanthropy reflected the confidence of supporters to the university’s mission.
“Their generosity is an investment in our students and our academic excellence,” Wilson said in the release. “We couldn’t do nearly as much without them.”

Israeli Startup Edelbyte Raises $70 Million to Enter Data Infrastructure Market
Founded by four Microsoft veterans, the company is targeting established players including Snowflake and Databricks as AI drives demand for faster, more affordable data analytics
Mandi Kogosowski
|
15/11/2026
Sponsored
Illustration: Kampus Production via pexels.com
Israeli startup Edelbyte has emerged from stealth with $70 million in seed and Series A funding to compete in the data infrastructure market, targeting established providers including Snowflake, Databricks, and ClickHouse.
Founded in 2025 by four former Microsoft engineers, the company is developing a search and analytics platform designed to help enterprises handle growing data volumes and AI-driven workloads without significantly increasing infrastructure costs.
The funding round was led by Sequoia and Quiet Capital, with participation from Greenoaks and Swish Ventures .
Edelbyte's founders – Avner Aharoni, Evgeney Ryzhyk, Alexander Sloutsky, and Yoni Leibowitz – each spent approximately 20 years at Microsoft, where they worked on Kusto, the data engine used across multiple Microsoft products.
The company is addressing a growing challenge for enterprises: AI applications and agents generate increasing numbers of queries across large datasets, putting additional pressure on infrastructure and budgets. Companies often respond by limiting queries, archiving data, or investing in additional capacity.
Edelbyte says its platform can help reduce these costs while supporting higher query volumes. Some customers migrating from existing systems have reportedly been able to run up to ten times more queries within the same budget.
Despite being founded less than two years ago, the company says it already has Fortune 500 customers running petabyte-scale deployments.
Based in Tel Aviv and San Francisco, Edelbyte plans to use the funding to expand its enterprise customer base, international operations, and workforce.
